Overview

What family law covers

Family law covers the legal side of relationships and family life: ending a marriage or civil partnership, dividing finances, making arrangements for children, and seeking protection where there is abuse or a risk of harm.

We explain each option open to you, what it is likely to cost and what happens next, so you can make decisions with a clear view of the road ahead.

How we can help

  • Explain your options in plain English
  • Negotiate with the other party or their solicitor
  • Prepare and draft agreements, applications and consent orders
  • Represent you in proceedings
  • Make urgent applications where protection is needed

Laws we work with

  • Matrimonial Causes Act 1973
  • Divorce, Dissolution and Separation Act 2020
  • Children Act 1989
  • Family Law Act 1996
  • 1980 Hague Convention
If you are in immediate danger, call 999.We can make urgent applications for protection, such as non-molestation and occupation orders. Contact us as soon as you are safe to do so.

Who we help

Parents

FAQs

Common questions

How much will my family matter cost?

It depends on the type of matter and whether it can be agreed. Before we start, we give you a fixed fee or a written estimate and explain what is and is not included. Court fees are separate. Published prices for family matters are being finalised and will appear on our Fees page.

Will my case have to go to court?

Not always. Many family matters are resolved by agreement, which can then be recorded in a court order. We will explain whether proceedings are likely in your circumstances and why.

Can we meet by video?

Yes. Appointments are available by phone, by video call or in person.

What should I bring to a first meeting?

Any letters or court papers you have received, details of any dates or deadlines, and a short note of the key events. We will tell you if we need anything else.
